problem_description: Single-item, periodic-review inventory control with deterministic lead time and lost sales. Time is indexed by periods t=1,...,L+T. Lead time is L periods: an order placed at the start of period t arrives at the start of period t+L. There is a planning phase with no demand and no cost (t=1,...,L) and a selling phase with demand and costs (t=L+1,...,L+T). The objective is to find a stationary ordering policy that minimizes the average total (holding + lost-sales) cost over the selling phase across N historical demand trajectories.

initial_state.Q_1: vector of length L with all zeros

state_definition.Q_t: pipeline_orders, length L, ordered oldest->newest; q_{t,1} arrives at start of period t, q_{t,k} arrives at start of period t+k-1

action_definition.a_t: order quantity placed at start of period t, >= 0; arrives at start of period t+L

demand_definition.D_t: exogenous demand in period t; D_t=0 for t<=L (planning phase); for evaluation, demands follow N historical trajectories (D_1^n,...,D_{L+T}^n)

within_period_timeline: 1) Arrival: receive q_{t,1} (the first element of Q_t). Available inventory before demand is I_t + q_{t,1}.
2) Ordering: choose action a_t = pi(I_t, Q_t) with a_t >= 0.
4) Sales / lost sales: S_t = min(I_t + q_{t,1}, D_t); LS_t = max(0, D_t - I_t - q_{t,1}).
5) Inventory transition: I_{t+1} = max(0, I_t + q_{t,1} - D_t).

policy_class.stationary_policy: pi maps state (I_t, Q_t) to action a_t; depends only on current (I_t,Q_t) and not on time or past history

objective.evaluation_metric: average total cost over selling periods across N trajectories
